message:
Plain words: the whole machine sits comfortably inside the weight limit with room for fixes. The 2025 NASA Lunabotics First Place Finish machine at 120 lb mass from the Sebastion | Engineering (E39) and the same win from the Sebastion | Engineering (E40) shows a 50 kg class digger is buildable, and the mass sum against the 60 kg limit (E41) is 47.0 kg leaving 13.0 kg margin, about a fifth of an adult body weight spare, so everyday scale says the limit is met.

Plain words: the battery carries a full work period and the dig motor only gets warm to the touch. A pack with Nominal Voltage 24V and Rated Capacity 10Ah from the batteria del fosfato del ferro del litio di 24V 10AH per il robot elettrico nella dimensione leggera e compatta from China Factory (E35) and with Nominal Voltage 24V and Rated Capacity 10Ah from the pacchetto della batteria di 24V 10AH LiFePO4 per il robot elettrico nella dimensione leggera e compatta from China Factory (E36) means two in parallel give 24.0 V 20.0 Ah for 480 Wh, where Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, meaning a safe long-life rechargeable chemistry) is the chemistry, and the motor heating estimate (E44) rises only 18.0 K after 300 s at 45.0 W waste heat, which is warm skin not boiling water, so everyday scale says heating is gentle.

Plain words: my frame stiffness check fails and must be fixed before building. 6061 T6 aluminum has a yield strength of 40 KSI at room temperature from the Engineering help please (E37) and 6061-T6 will allow up to around 15,000 psi working stress from the Aluminum square tubing strength (E38), where KSI means thousand pounds per square inch and psi means pounds per square inch, but the single-rail cantilever deflection estimate (E43) gives 72.9 mm sag under full weight, a hand width and far above millimetre wobble, so Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead and Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead please note the tube size or twin-rail sharing must be stiffened. Not ready, because the frame concept does not yet survive its own deflection check.
